prompt: Explain how U.S. health insurance works using only fantasy football metaphors. Keep going long after the metaphor collapses.
response:
To understand the U.S. healthcare system, simply imagine you are joining a very expensive, deeply confusing fantasy football league. 

First, just to be in the league, you have to pay the Commissioner a massive entry fee every single week. This is your **Premium**. It doesn’t matter if your team is undefeated or if you finish dead last; you pay this fee just for the privilege of keeping the app on your phone.

Now, let’s say your starting Quarterback gets statistically crushed in a game. You want to pick up a free agent off the waiver wire to heal your roster. But wait! You can’t just use the players' points right away. First, you have to hit your **Deductible**. This means you must personally spot your opponent 5,000 points out of your own total before your players' touchdowns actually count for anything. Until your team gives up those 5,000 points, you are entirely responsible for every fumble.

Even after you hit that threshold, every time you make a roster move or click on a player's profile (go to the doctor), the app charges you a flat $40 fee. This is your **Copay**. 

You also have to be careful about who you draft. Your Commissioner has given you a specific list of approved players—these are your **In-Network** providers. If you draft a starting running back from this list, it’s mostly covered.
